title: Frame skills as resisting manipulation
statement: For adolescents, pitch a reading skill as a way to resist being manipulated, catching how a text works on the reader, rather than as practice of a skill.
example: In a double-blind trial with 536 eighth graders, healthy eating framed as standing up to food-industry manipulation beat standard health education.
detail: The Grade 9 research brief reports a double-blind randomized trial with 536 eighth graders in which framing healthy eating as standing up to food-industry manipulation beat standard health education, and students made healthier choices a day later in an unrelated setting. It rates this as one strong randomized trial, in health rather than reading, and draws the pitch for close reading: catch how the text works on you, not 'let's practice our skill'. The Grade 9 strategy adopts that pitch.
against: One trial, in healthy eating rather than reading (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/learners-voice-guide.md`, line 20); whether the framing helps reading is untested.

evidence.quote: In a double-blind randomized trial with 536 eighth graders, framing healthy eating as standing up to food-industry manipulation beat standard health education.
Do not pitch it as "let's practice our skill."
Close reading can be pitched the same way: catch how the text is working on you.
